rubric: Classify only whether the supplied excerpt supports, contradicts or is insufficient to determine the exact claim. A true claim absent from the excerpt is insufficient. Absence of evidence is not proof of absence.
design: 6 verified official-page excerpts × 3 independently prelabelled claims; split=3 development sources and 3 held-out sources; all gold labels established before any model calls

cases.source_excerpt: Earth and the Moon are an average of 384,400 kilometers (238,855 miles) apart.
cases.claim: The Moon's average distance from Earth is about 384,400 kilometres.
cases.gold_rationale: The passage explicitly states the average distance in kilometers.

cases.source_excerpt: Earth and the Moon are an average of 384,400 kilometers (238,855 miles) apart.
cases.claim: Die durchschnittliche Entfernung des Mondes beträgt laut Beleg 84.400 Kilometer.
cases.gold_rationale: The quoted average Earth-Moon distance is 384,400 km, not 84,400 km.

cases.source_excerpt: Earth and the Moon are an average of 384,400 kilometers (238,855 miles) apart.
cases.claim: This excerpt establishes that the Moon takes 27.3 days to complete one orbit.
cases.gold_rationale: Orbital period is not given in the supplied passage.

cases.source_title: How much water is in the ocean?
cases.source_excerpt: The ocean covers more than 70 percent of the surface of our planet.
cases.claim: More than 70 percent of Earth's surface is covered by the ocean.
cases.gold_rationale: The passage explicitly asserts more than 70 percent surface coverage.

cases.source_title: How much water is in the ocean?
cases.source_excerpt: The ocean covers more than 70 percent of the surface of our planet.
cases.claim: Weniger als die Hälfte der Erdoberfläche ist vom Ozean bedeckt.
cases.gold_rationale: More than 70 percent contradicts less than one half.

cases.source_title: How much water is in the ocean?
cases.source_excerpt: The ocean covers more than 70 percent of the surface of our planet.
cases.claim: According to this passage, the Pacific is the world's largest ocean by area.
cases.gold_rationale: This passage gives only total ocean coverage, not individual ocean areas.

cases.source_title: 2020 Census Apportionment Results Delivered to the President
cases.source_excerpt: the 2020 Census shows the resident population of the United States on April 1, 2020, was 331,449,281.
cases.claim: The quoted 2020 Census resident count for the United States on April 1, 2020 is 331,449,281.
cases.gold_rationale: The passage contains the same population, geography, and date.

cases.source_title: 2020 Census Apportionment Results Delivered to the President
cases.source_excerpt: the 2020 Census shows the resident population of the United States on April 1, 2020, was 331,449,281.
cases.claim: The quoted U.S. resident population on April 1, 2020 was 301,449,281.

cases.source_title: 2020 Census Apportionment Results Delivered to the President
cases.source_excerpt: the 2020 Census shows the resident population of the United States on April 1, 2020, was 331,449,281.
cases.claim: The quoted Census excerpt confirms an increase of 7.4 percent from 2010.
cases.gold_rationale: The excerpt itself contains no previous comparison or growth percentage.

cases.source_title: Earthquake Magnitude, Energy Release, and Shaking Intensity
cases.source_excerpt: each whole number increase in magnitude represents a tenfold increase in measured amplitude as measured on a seismogram.
cases.claim: A one-unit increase in earthquake magnitude corresponds to ten times the measured seismic amplitude.
cases.gold_rationale: The excerpt explicitly states a tenfold increase in measured amplitude.

cases.source_title: Earthquake Magnitude, Energy Release, and Shaking Intensity
cases.source_excerpt: each whole number increase in magnitude represents a tenfold increase in measured amplitude as measured on a seismogram.
cases.claim: Bei einer Magnitudenzunahme um eine Einheit verdoppelt sich die gemessene Amplitude.
cases.gold_rationale: The excerpt states tenfold rather than twofold amplitude growth.

cases.source_title: Earthquake Magnitude, Energy Release, and Shaking Intensity
cases.source_excerpt: each whole number increase in magnitude represents a tenfold increase in measured amplitude as measured on a seismogram.
cases.claim: The passage demonstrates that each magnitude increase releases exactly ten times as much energy.
cases.gold_rationale: It describes measured amplitude, not the energy-release ratio.

cases.source_title: NIST Guide to the SI — Appendix A
cases.source_excerpt: The second is the duration of 9 192 631 770 periods of the radiation
cases.claim: A second corresponds to 9,192,631,770 periods of the radiation referred to in this definition.
cases.gold_rationale: The number of radiation periods matches the source wording.

cases.source_title: NIST Guide to the SI — Appendix A
cases.source_excerpt: The second is the duration of 9 192 631 770 periods of the radiation
cases.claim: The passage defines a second using 9,192,631,771 periods of radiation.

cases.source_title: NIST Guide to the SI — Appendix A
cases.source_excerpt: The second is the duration of 9 192 631 770 periods of the radiation
cases.claim: The passage identifies the emitting atom as cesium-133.
cases.gold_rationale: No chemical element or isotope is named in this excerpt.

cases.source_excerpt: The many missions that have explored the Moon have found no evidence to suggest it has its own living things.
cases.claim: Die erwähnten Mondmissionen haben keine Hinweise auf dortiges eigenes Leben gefunden.
cases.gold_rationale: The source reports no evidence found by those missions, not absolute absence.

cases.source_excerpt: The many missions that have explored the Moon have found no evidence to suggest it has its own living things.
cases.claim: The missions mentioned discovered positive evidence that the Moon harbors its own living things.
cases.gold_rationale: The excerpt states they have found no such evidence.

cases.source_excerpt: The many missions that have explored the Moon have found no evidence to suggest it has its own living things.
cases.claim: The quoted missions prove that no living organism exists anywhere on the Moon.
cases.gold_rationale: Absence of found evidence does not establish exhaustive absence of life.
